subject: Oceanography
title: Oil Spills
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Oil Spills.

hook.text: The Deepwater Horizon spill released 4.9 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico over 87 days.

buildup.text: Oil spreads as a slick on the surface—blocking light, coating wildlife, and poisoning the water column.

discovery.text: Dispersants break oil into tiny droplets—making it less visible but more available to marine organisms.

twist.text: Much of the oil sank to the seafloor—creating a toxic layer that still affects deep-sea life over a decade later.

climax.text: Despite cleanup technology, only 10–15% of spilled oil is typically recovered—nature does most of the work.

punchline.text: We can spill millions of barrels—but can only clean up a fraction.

quiz.question: How much spilled oil is typically recovered during cleanup?
